about: The open FOCUS_Spec issues and pull requests that concern each dataset and column, matched by the files they change and the names in their titles and descriptions, rebuilt daily from GitHub. Each thread's summary is written by an AI model from the thread, or reused from the History or Recent summaries, and rewritten when the thread gains comments or reviews. The summaries paraphrase those discussions and name participants by their GitHub usernames.

975.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this feature request for a normalized recommendations dataset, because practitioners receive optimization recommendations such as rightsizing and commitment purchases from many providers in different formats; eleven organizations backed it. In 2026 the work moved to task force 2 through #2444, and the thread recorded decisions there: evaluation period start and end columns with duration deferred, past-participle date column names, and RecommendationProviderName in place of DataGeneratorName. flanakin and rileyjenk disagreed over resource configuration columns, and the scope was trimmed before initial Member review in September 2026. In October 2026 maintainers moved the dataset and its supported feature, #2583, to the 1.6 cycle for lack of consensus on its shape and names. The request remained open.

1027.title: [FR] Rename "Charge" row term to just "Row"
1027.author: rileyjenk
1027.summary: Issue #1027, opened by rileyjenk for Domo, proposes replacing the glossary term "Charge" for dataset rows with plain "Row". The concern is that charge already means a financial charge in FinOps, so it reads oddly for rows that are not charges. The requester sees low impact, since it is only terminology, though it would need revisiting if FOCUS moved to a JSON-oriented dataset. Recently kk09v noted that the SKU Price dataset already uses "record" for the same concept, and that charge and record are both verbs as well as nouns. They seem to favour row, as it is unlikely to be used as an action in the specification. No one has pushed back, but there is no decision or further reaction yet, so the issue looks to be waiting on the working group.

With kk09v and qquigley as sponsors and work starting in 1.4, TF-2 widened it from resource to charge tagging after cnharris10 noted SaaS tags without resources, and ruled out SKUs as the basis. From eleven candidate structures the group chose a key-driven TagDetails column alongside Tags, after kk09v's BigQuery tests, drafted as #1904. 1974.summary: Issue #1974, opened by ljadvey in February 2026, asks that worked examples in the FOCUS specification pass the FOCUS Validator, since implementers use them as templates. Checks against 1.2 found missing MUST columns, numeric-looking IDs, null conditional values, non-conforming PricingUnit values and provider mismatches. It has been marked Seeking Champion since 31 October 2026. The 11 November 2026 TF2 update says PR #2558 adds a validator check for commitment discount flexibility examples, skipping rules known to fail by mistake, and stays open for 1.6. Open PRs #2661 and #2662 bring SaaS and commitment discount examples to the 1.3 schema; one participant offered to close them, while another asked that nothing close while authors are still being asked. Little discussion beyond the update suggests progress depends on qquigley finishing #2558 if it stalls.

2174.title: [FR] Distinguish data originators, processors, and intermediaries
2174.author: Matt-Cowsert
2174.summary: This request asks the working group to separate the roles hidden behind data generator, which covers both the providers that create billing data and the FinOps tools that process it, so each requirement says who it applies to. It also wants lineage showing who last changed a row and where it came from, plus a marketplace seller case in the participating entity appendix. Several maintainers stress the last party to touch the data, while others note data can start outside FOCUS. One maintainer doubts the problem statement holds as written, so the Maintainers could not rate the request. Participants disagree on whether lineage needs metadata FRs #1060 and #1131 first. On 16 November 2026 the Maintainers agreed to open a new FR defining the entities, with lineage after it, so this request's future looks unsettled.

2437.title: [FR] Distinguish AI inference processing tiers
2437.author: Matt-Cowsert
2437.summary: This request asks for a standard way to record which processing tier an AI charge was billed under, such as Standard, Priority or Batch, since providers price the same model differently by tier. Practitioners cannot currently compare tiers or spot non-urgent workloads that could move to batch without provider-specific parsing. thecloudman has championed it and opened #2873, targeting 1.6, which adds a ProcessingTier property with five values: Standard, Priority, Flex, Batch and Other. Flex goes beyond the three proposed values because several providers price it separately. It also keeps PricingCategory at Standard and excludes provisioned capacity from #2371. Open questions for Task Force 2 cover the value set, provisioned capacity and whether the tier sits on the SKU or the SKU Price. No replies yet, so the thread looks early.

Task force 2 renamed Currency to RecommendationCurrency after shawnalpay asked for a prefix. Merges with working_draft dropped and then duplicated a section of data_model.md, and thecloudman found links that would break; these were fixed. shawnalpay named two threads as blocking in September 2026, and the pull request was still open after its October 2026 activity.

It remained open, last active in August 2026.

2613.title: FR #2414: Region scope as a SkuPriceDetails property
2613.author: Matt-Cowsert
2613.summary:
Matt-Cowsert opened #2613 on 10 August 2026 to implement FR #2414 by adding a FOCUS-defined region scope property to SkuPriceDetails, with example values "Global", "Regional" and "DataZone", a footnote separating it from RegionId and Redundancy, and an appendix example. It was drafted as ServingScope.

Reviewers questioned the name: flanakin and marc-perreaut found "serving" unclear, and udam-stitcher and mike-finopsorg backed GeographicScope. ijurica wanted pricing framing dropped, and qquigley objected to an undefined population rule. Matt-Cowsert amended the footnote and argued PricingRegionId cannot close the gap. After flanakin's research (#2672), RegionScope was settled on 17 September, and #2667 merged into the branch on 23 September. jpradocueva's validation passed. On 18 November, jerrysr99 asked whether SKU versus SKU Price placement should be decided once. The PR remains open.

2706.title: [FR] Expose the unit price a commitment discount buys on covered usage
2706.author: Matt-Cowsert
2706.summary: Matt-Cowsert asks for a field giving the per-unit rate a commitment discount buys on each covered charge. Today that rate appears only as a cost. EffectiveCost mixes in other reductions, and ContractedUnitPrice reflects a negotiated discount rather than the commitment, so no column holds the rate the commitment set. Providers differ: AWS rates shift with payment model, while Azure and Google Cloud hold them flat, so the definition must allow a value equal to the contracted rate. The open question is placement, Cost and Usage or SKU Price, and whether draft #2753 resolves it. A TF2 update on 4 November 2026 keeps it open under #2807 while ijurica checks the problem against #2753 and Matt-Cowsert and flanakin plan how related requests split. No reactions beyond that update are visible yet, so support and objections are not on record.

2832.title: [Editorial] Correct the Contract Commitment and commitment program examples for the 1.5 release
2832.author: Matt-Cowsert
2832.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this editorial issue on 5 November 2026 to correct examples, data and descriptions in the 1.5 specification that don't match its own requirements or allowed values. It gathers findings from a full review of 1.5 done on 4 November 2026, plus similar cases the author found. The fixes are all informative text: wrong ServiceCategory and ServiceSubcategory values such as Database and No-SQL DB, a non-FOCUS dimension named UsageType, a discount formula that omits commitment discounts, and capacity reservations wrongly described as discount-bearing. Most also affect the published 1.4 specification. Because they are editorial, they can merge into working_draft during the 1.5 IP Review, which ends 1 December 2026. No discussion appears yet, so there is no visible disagreement, but nobody has confirmed the fixes. The description is truncated in this digest.

2833.title: [Editorial] Correct the split cost allocation and commitment discount examples for the 1.5 release
2833.author: Matt-Cowsert
2833.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 5 November 2026 to collect wrong numbers and values in 1.5 appendix examples, found in a full review of the specification. One commitment discount example uses VM_LARGE factor 4 instead of the catalog's 3, which changes the covered share and on-demand cost. A CrestNode monthly fee is annual divided by 12 rather than hourly rate times 672 hours. Fourteen files use 'Compute Instances', which is not an allowed ServiceSubcategory value. A split cost allocation example leaves AllocatedServiceName null on a retained origin row, breaking the requirement from #2655. All fixes change informative text and example data, so they can merge into working_draft during the 1.5 IP Review, which ends 1 December 2026. The CrestNode amount depends on #2716, and the requirement wording stays in #2515. No comments yet, so reaction is unknown.

2834.title: [Editorial] Correct the metadata links, key names, and examples for the 1.5 release
2834.author: Matt-Cowsert
2834.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened #2834 on 5 November 2026 to correct links, key names and examples in the Metadata section of the 1.5 specification. Most problems are wrong links, key names that differ from the defined ones such as RecencyLastUpdate, nonexistent dataset names such as FOCUS Contract, and examples reusing one SchemaId. The fixes change only informative text, so they can merge into working_draft during the 1.5 IP Review, which ends 1 December 2026, and most also apply to the published 1.4 specification. No one has commented yet, so there is no sign of support or objection; the only activity is status housekeeping. The digest cuts off the description, so the list may be longer. If accepted, 1.5 readers get working links and examples that match the defined keys, with no change to normative rules.

2835.title: [Editorial] Correct summary tables, glossary entries, labels, and links for the 1.5 release
2835.author: Matt-Cowsert
2835.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this editorial issue on 5 November 2026 to gather corrections from a full review of the 1.5 specification, plus similar cases found while checking it. The fixes change only informative text: a summary table wrongly says Host Provider Name does not allow nulls (1.4 says it does, and the error crept in through a later merge), a Billing Currency link points to the wrong place, preview labels are wrong, and there are glossary, property, relationship and section-order slips. Because the editorial IP Review process applies, these can merge into working_draft now and join the release when the review ends on 1 December 2026. Nobody has commented yet, so there is no visible support or objection. Order and row changes are to be done last.

2836.title: [Feedback] Correct casing, IDs, and links in 1.5 requirement text
2836.author: Matt-Cowsert
2836.summary: This issue gathers nine small fixes from a review of the 1.5 requirement text: casing of MUST NOT and null, Id versus ID in metadata names, a wrong column reference in InvoiceDetailId, a label naming AllocationMethod (which is not a column), and a rename that changes a published anchor. Matt-Cowsert, who opened it, says none change what a requirement asks and proposed holding them for 1.5 as errata. A later comment from Matt-Cowsert says the Maintainers agreed to apply them as editorial improvements to working_draft instead. That comment dates the meeting to 2027, which looks like a typo for 2026. It does not say whether the anchor rename in row 9 was kept. No other reactions yet, so the item looks agreed on the Maintainers' side but is still open.

2837.title: [Feedback] Correct the Payment Currency, Contract ID, and Time Sector End requirements
2837.author: Matt-Cowsert
2837.summary: Matt-Cowsert filed this from a review of the 1.5 specification on 4 November 2026, which found three requirement lines that don't match their definitions. The first would add a Currency Format requirement to PaymentCurrency, matching BillingCurrency, which the requirements model currently lacks. The second drops a redundant condition on ContractId not being null, since the line already requires that, so nothing required changes, though the requirements model needs a matching change too. The third concerns a lowercase must in TimeSectorEnd, which is not a BCP-14 keyword and so is not normative today; Maintainers need to decide whether it is a typo or needs a feature request. Nobody has commented yet, so there is no read on support. The item is open and sits in the 1.5 errata bundle. Separate informative fixes #2832 to #2835 merge during IP Review.

2838.title: [Maintenance] State how repeated [*] paths bind to array elements in JSON object requirements
2838.author: finops-DaveMoreau
2838.summary: DaveMoreau opened this to flag JSON Object Format requirements that use several [*] paths, or pair a [*] subject with a quantifier, without saying whether the paths refer to the same array element. The guidelines do not settle repeated wildcards, and RFC 9535 would allow either reading. Cases fall into three groups: same element meant but unstated (contractapplied, allocatedmethoddetails); different elements meant, with scope to confirm for the ContractCommitmentId pairing, possibly tied to #2701; and a 'one' versus every-element quantifier mismatch. The proposed fix is an explicit qualifier in each requirement. Matt-Cowsert notes #2827 has dropped its qualifier, leaving Requester Details unqualified, and asks for those lines in the same-element table. No other replies yet, so support looks limited to the author and that commenter. The issue is open with no decision recorded.

2839.title: [FR] Clarify Tier and Tiered Terminology in the Specification
2839.author: ijurica
2839.summary: Issue #2839, opened by ijurica on 5 November 2026, says 'tier' and 'tiered' mean several different things in the specification: pricing by quantity, spend or duration, tiered commitment discounts, storage tiers and SaaS feature tiers. The minimum ask is glossary terms for the tiered pricing concepts, with ambiguous mentions reworded and linked to them; an appendix on how the concepts relate is a possible follow-up. It builds on PR #2564, an earlier unmerged attempt from the 1.5 cycle, and notes that FR #2739 and PR #2748 could use the new terms. If it goes ahead, practitioners could tell from a column definition which pricing model is meant. Nobody has commented yet, so the working group's view of the scope or wording is unknown. The issue remains open with no decision or next step recorded.

2840.title: AI #2825: Add 1.5 Changelog
2840.author: Matt-Cowsert
2840.summary: This PR adds the v1.5 section to CHANGELOG.md, built from the diff between v1.4 and v1.5-cr rather than milestone titles so each entry traces to the specification text. It is part of #2825 and does not close it, since the Contributors list is tracked in #2830. The section is organised by Change Impact Classification, and the classifications, including six Migration Compatible changes, are the main thing to check. shawnalpay verified the counts and requested classification and wording fixes, which Matt-Cowsert has applied in a new commit. flanakin suggested dropping one adjective, and davidearney, flanakin and finops-DaveMoreau have approved, giving three approvals. Entries for the IP Review editorial fixes will be added as each merges. Substantive questions appear resolved, so the remaining work is those editorial entries.

2841.title: [AI] Add 1.4 to 1.5 version migration guidance
2841.author: Matt-Cowsert
2841.summary: Matt-Cowsert asks for a FOCUS 1.4 to 1.5 section in the version migration guidance, modelled on the 1.3 to 1.4 section (#1548, #1597) and placed above it. It would be built from the v1.5 changelog (#2840) and a diff between the published 1.4 spec and the 1.5 release candidate. For people producing or consuming FOCUS data, it would cover each Migration Compatible change, the operating model conditions now governing column presence, and renames to the anchor and requirements models that affect tooling. It would also state that the SKU Price preview is excluded from conformance. The target is a pull request approved by Members before the working group approves v1.5 on 3 December 2026. No one has replied yet, so support or objections are unknown, and the thread looks quiet since opening on 6 November 2026.

2842.title: AI #2841: Add 1.4 to 1.5 migration guide
2842.author: Matt-Cowsert
2842.summary: Matt-Cowsert's PR (#2842) adds a 1.4 to 1.5 section to the migration guidance, implementing #2841 in the same layout as the 1.3 to 1.4 section. The core point is that 1.5 removes or renames no columns and changes no types or nullability, so the impact is on values: queries can run cleanly yet return different results. Beyond the five Migration Compatible changes, it covers revised presence rules for data generators and two renames affecting tools. It also states that the SKU Price preview is optional, not checked for conformance, and may change without notice. The PR was opened on 6 November 2026 and has no review activity yet, so reception is unclear. It depends on #2840 merging first, and needs Member approval before the WG approves v1.5 on 3 December 2026.

2843.title: FR #2782: Define the preview lifecycle for whole datasets

2843.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this draft pull request as a starting point for feature request #2782, which asks how a whole-dataset preview moves to stable or is removed, since the merged rules only cover its start. It adds markers to the Preview Process in the spec change guidelines: Proposed answers where existing evidence supports one, and TODO markers elsewhere. Proposals cover supporting entities, the scope list rule for requirements, and which Version Introduced value shows after promotion, and drafted text covers four questions. Nothing merges until the Task Force settles each answer. No approvals, change requests or comments are recorded yet, so reaction is not visible. The description says Task Force 1 took it up on 10 November 2026, but the record shows the change to TF-Core 1 that day, so its placement looks unsettled.

It is built from the 1.5 release candidate and adds the preview SKU Price dataset (23 columns), four Cost and Usage columns, and operating model conditions replacing free-text conditions and the Applicability Criteria tab. 2849.title: [AI] Track the 1.5 errata from Maintainer assessment to one errata PR
2849.author: Matt-Cowsert
2849.summary: This Action Item tracks the 1.5 errata candidates, filed as separate Feedback issues, from Maintainer assessment to one errata PR against working_draft, merged after 1.5 is published. Three are listed: #2836 corrects casing, IDs and links in 1.5 requirement text; #2837 corrects the PaymentCurrency, ContractId and TimeSectorEnd requirements; and #2783 points out that two CAU commitment discount requirements have no Condition, so a null value fails them, also in 1.2 to 1.4. Under the Errata Guidelines, changes to BCP-14 keywords, added columns or properties, or validation logic go to Feature Request instead. An open question is whether SkuPrice rules should join the 1.5 model through errata. The thread was opened by Matt-Cowsert on 10 November 2026 with no comments or assessments yet, so support can't be judged; all three candidates still await Maintainer assessment.

2850.title: [AI] Compare SKU Price dataset columns with SkuPriceDetails properties
2850.author: Matt-Cowsert
2850.summary: This issue asks for a two-way check of SKU Price dataset columns against FOCUS-defined SkuPriceDetails properties. It follows a TF1 discussion: SkuPriceDetails is meant to describe what matters for a SKU, not its price tiers, yet context window size sits apart from AI properties such as model family. jerrysr99 posted the comparison on 16 November, listing 25 SKU Price columns and 21 properties, with only the two context window bounds from #2521 appearing in both. The list is a snapshot; it does not yet say which gaps should close, and no one has responded since. If the group proceeds, Matt-Cowsert expects one feature request per column added, as with the model family and token direction properties. One participant warned that carrying every column would keep SkuPriceDetails growing. Results go to TF1 on 17 November.

2851.title: [AI] Reword "term" in the Commitment Discount Quantity requirement
2851.author: Matt-Cowsert
2851.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue after a #2773 review found that "term" in the Commitment Discount Quantity requirement is ambiguous. It means how long the commitment discount runs, which the introduction calls its period, yet the glossary defines Term as an agreement on a contract or invoice. A reviewer removed the glossary link, but the wording stayed because rewording a normative requirement was out of scope for an editorial PR. The options are keeping "term" as plain English, or rewording it to "period", the closer fit, which changes requirement text. That means it cannot merge into the working draft during the 1.5 IP Review, so it moves to the 1.6 cycle. The first step searches the specification for other requirements using "term" for a duration. No one has commented yet, so the group's leaning is unclear.

2852.title: [AI] Decide how the Columns table and the Requirements column list count for first-occurrence linking
2852.author: Matt-Cowsert
2852.summary: This issue asks whether the Columns table and the Requirements column list in dataset files count toward the rule that an entity is linked only on its first occurrence. It arose in PR #2773, where a new Relationships link repeated a term already linked in the table and list, and was removed. The open choices are whether the table counts, which would make the list link the repeat, and whether the list needs its own exception, since linking every column there is existing practice. The Members meeting on 29 October 2026 agreed to follow the guidelines as written and revisit linking in 1.6. Only the opening post exists so far, so support or pushback can't be read yet. Next, the group must decide and record why, then a draft PR updates the guidelines and AGENTS.md.

2853.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened #2853 on 11 November 2026 as an editorial pull request closing #2833 and the open items in #2655. It corrects appendix examples, example CSVs and a query whose numbers contradicted their own data or a requirement, with no requirement changes. thecloudman and jpradocueva suggested wording fixes and raised a ConsumedQuantity question, which Matt-Cowsert resolved. 2854.title: [AI] Revisit the SKU Price Description column
2854.author: ijurica
2854.summary: ijurica opened this issue because the introduction and Description section of the SKU Price Description column conflict over whether it describes the SKU Price construct or a single SKU Price record. The CSV examples treat it as record-level, since it changes between records under one SKU Price ID. The working group is asked to choose a reading and align the definition and examples. Choosing the construct reading raises further questions about whether descriptions must match across records of one ID and differ between IDs of the same provider. Rewording alone would not settle it, since the column is described as self-contained and as adding information not otherwise available. For producers and users of FOCUS data, the answer changes what a value describes. Nobody has responded since opening on 11 November 2026, so support is unclear.

2855.title: [AI] Align pricing terminology across the SKU Price dataset, its appendix, and its supported features
2855.author: ijurica
2855.summary: ijurica opened this issue on 11 November 2026 to align pricing terms across the SKU Price dataset, its appendix and supported features, after a TF-2 update flagged several meanings of rate. The aim is precise wording: unit price for a value, SKU Price for the stable construct, SKU Price record for a single row where effective period, currency or contract matters, and price list instead of rate card. Some edits may change what a requirement applies to, such as IsGlobalScope in #2735, so the author wants those flagged separately in the pull request, and lines overlapping open PR #2845 left alone. For FOCUS data users the effect would be clearer wording, with a few requirements possibly shifting in scope. The thread has no comments yet, so the group's view is unknown. No pull request exists yet.

2856.title: [AI] Clarify distinction between `SKU Price` construct and `SKU Price` records
2856.author: ijurica
2856.summary: ijurica opened this issue on 11 November 2026 to question the shared name SKU Price, used for both the construct identified by SKU Price ID and the dataset whose rows are records, where one ID spans several records. The case is that the dataset name implies one row per SKU Price, unlike Contract Commitment, and that normative requirements need the word record to avoid ambiguity, which has already caused confusion in the specification. Options are keeping the name, renaming only the dataset, or renaming it along with record-level columns such as SkuPriceEffectiveStart, since renaming the dataset alone would not change those. A rename would touch the dataset, columns, examples and preview notes, and is possible because the dataset is still preview. No one has replied yet, so the group's view is unknown.

2860.title: [AI] Add semantic tag tooling to the specification build
2860.author: finops-DaveMoreau
2860.summary: finops-DaveMoreau opened this action item to bring the semantic tag tooling from the #2779 demo into the specification build, with no change to specification content. Tags such as column and term references are resolved to today's link and italics conventions and checked; the registry and resolver come with tests. The change is meant to be backwards compatible: with no tags the output stays identical, and tagged and hand-written links can coexist. Converting the specification would follow in separate reviewable steps, each recording conversion progress per tag kind. Two open decisions are flagged, on tool location and whether spec.md resolves tags before Pandoc; the description cuts off there. Opened 12 November 2026 and marked critical path. No comments or reactions yet, so the working group's view is not visible.

2861.title: [AI] Decide the conversion and rendering rules for semantic tags
2861.author: finops-DaveMoreau
2861.summary: Opened by finops-DaveMoreau on 12 November 2026 under #2779, this issue writes down the rules for converting the specification to semantic tags, so the Working Group approves each rule once rather than reviewing 300-plus files line by line. Conversion rules decide which text becomes which tag; rendering rules decide how tags appear in the published specification, so they touch every tag. Translations carry over existing markup, wrong links included, and account for 6,841 tags in 332 files. Inferences go further: plain Display Name matching adds 866 tags in 231 files, with Title Case words meaning a concept rather than a column as the main risk. Each rule becomes a separate converter switch, and later conversion PRs would be checked only against approved rules. Nobody has commented yet, so there is no reaction to read; the issue depends on #2860.

2862.title: [AI] Convert existing references to semantic tags with the translation rules
2862.author: finops-DaveMoreau
2862.summary: finops-DaveMoreau proposes running the translation rules approved in #2861 over the specification, converting entity links, italic glossary terms and plain entity IDs into semantic tags and marking each kind as mechanical so CI keeps it converted. The conversion copies what the markup says now and corrects nothing. A first mention that will link to the glossary rather than the record #2735 describes is left for a separate change. The proposal is one PR for every kind and file, timed with maintainers, with one PR per area as the alternative. It changes 689 rendered lines but no visible words, and leaves 234 items open, mostly ColumnIds defined in several datasets. Checks show no errors and 20 warnings that reflect existing source disagreements. The thread is new, opened 12 November 2026 and assigned to TF-Supporting, with no discussion or reaction yet.

2864.title: AI #2849: Add 1.5 errata
2864.author: Matt-Cowsert
2864.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this draft PR to set out the scope of the 1.5 errata tracked in #2849 for Maintainer assessment. It adds a Version 1.5 section to ERRATA.md with one row per correction from #2836, #2837 and #2783, so the Maintainers can assess them in final form. Nothing carries the errata label yet, and the PR merges only after 1.5 is published. Flagged for the Maintainers: whether the lowercase 'must' in row #3 is a typo or needs a Feature Request, whether the anchor rename in row #8 is worth breaking existing links, and that rows #13 and #14 stand or fall with rows #1 and #2. Section numbers, fix PRs and SkuPrice rules are left for later. No one has reacted yet, so the group's view is unknown and the PR awaits Maintainer assessment.

2866.title: [AI] Align FOCUS entity references and links in the spec with Contributor Guidelines
2866.author: ijurica
2866.summary: ijurica opened #2866 on 12 November 2026 to align entity references and links in three parts of the specification with the contributor guidelines: the SKU Price dataset, the appendix and supported features. These were skipped in #2772 and PR #2773 to avoid clashing with other open PRs. Focus areas are reference forms in normative requirements, Entity ID and Display Name formatting, first-occurrence linking and link targets. It is explicitly best-effort, so some references may stay unaligned, either pending discussion or following decisions not yet written into the guidelines. In practice this looks like editorial tidying rather than new requirements. The thread has no comments yet, so there is no visible support or pushback. The only stated completion point is a draft PR, which has not been opened yet.

2868.summary: This draft, opened by finops-DaveMoreau on 13 November 2026, brings the semantic tag tooling from the demo (#2819) into the specification build under #2779, with no content change. Tags name the entity a reference means and the build turns them into today's links and italics, checking each one. Untagged output should match the base branch byte for byte, so existing links keep working. Open questions are where the tools live, resolving tags before Pandoc, keeping REG016 a warning, and running REG017 before releases. Billing Period was converted in a scratch copy with small rendered differences, and tests pass locally. No one has commented or reviewed yet, so reception is unknown; it is still a draft that the conversions #2861 to #2863 depend on.

2871.title: FR #2521: Add context-window pricing properties to SKU Price Details
2871.author: jerrysr99
2871.summary:
Pull request #2871, opened by jerrysr99 on 14 November 2026, proposed adding ContextWindowMinimum and ContextWindowMaximum to SkuPriceDetails so practitioners can see which context-window pricing tier a charge used, without parsing provider text. It builds on FR #2521 and a 10 November Task Force 1 direction, with the SKU Price columns in #2872.

thecloudman reviewed it, and jerrysr99 applied most suggestions: SHOULD instead of MUST, the existing nullability rule restored, and the counting basis tied to each provider's own terms. The explicit null and boundary convention were left for Task Force 1. finops-DaveMoreau argued each tier should be its own SKU; jerrysr99 was open to it. Renaming the keys to TokenContextWindowMinimum and TokenContextWindowMaximum was agreed. Matt-Cowsert suggested wording fixes. As of 18 November 2026 the pull request was still open.

2872.title: FR #2521: Add context-window pricing columns to SKU Price (stacked on the properties PR)
2872.author: jerrysr99
2872.summary: jerrysr99 has opened this draft implementing the SKU Price part of FR #2521, which asks for long-context AI charges to be distinguished from standard-context charges for the same model. Google's Gemini models price at a 200K-token prompt threshold, and FOCUS data currently blends those rates together. The pull request adds two Conditional columns, ContextWindowMinimum (exclusive) and ContextWindowMaximum (inclusive), measured in input tokens per request, along with an IncludesContextWindowPricing condition, dataset requirements and an appendix example. Unlike Quantity Tier Minimum, the minimum is null when price does not vary by window size. It is stacked on #2871 and needs that branch first. Trial merges conflict with #2748, #2749 and #2753, which also edit the SKU Price column table. No reviews or approvals exist yet; the only other activity is jerrysr99's comment listing providers with context-window pricing.

The PR stayed open.

2877.title: [AI] Build a 1.6 example dataset for context window pricing
2877.author: Matt-Cowsert
2877.summary: Issue #2877 asks for a 1.6 example dataset showing how providers bill context window pricing, to support feature request #2521 and draft pull requests #2871 and #2872. The open point from the 17 November Task Force 1 meeting is the quantity columns: a billing row adds up many requests, often over an hour, so its token count is not one request's window. Google Cloud gives each tier its own SKU ID and AWS is expected to follow, while the CSVs in #2871 give both tiers one SkuId with separate SkuPriceIds. If it goes ahead, finops-DaveMoreau would show tiers in Cost and Usage rows with ConsumedQuantity, PricingQuantity and units, mirrored in the SKU Price dataset. No replies yet, so reaction is unclear. The issue is open due 24 November 2026 with the spreadsheet not yet shared with TF1.

2879.title: Add Azure practitioner scenarios to SKU Price supported features
2879.author: flanakin
2879.summary: This draft from flanakin, for issue #49, proposes spec-only rules for weighting portfolios: a FAANGMAN portfolio weighted by each name's share of SPY, and an equal-weight chips portfolio. Despite its Azure title, the body covers these weightings and a benchmark change. The FAANGMAN weight rule was already set on #49, but three points remain open: the Alphabet share class, whether to keep a 25% cap, and a 5% cash line. The benchmark would become unfiltered SPY for every portfolio, citing a 17 November 2026 sync; the comparison script still uses filtered SPY until approval. Portfolios would start on the first trading day after approval, with the cap effect reported apart from research effect. No reviews, approvals or comments exist yet, so this looks early-stage. It closes #49 only after both approvers sign off.
